findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T03] Credential Forwarding in chain.call_downstream
findings.detail: The tool forwards credentials directly, allowing an attacker to use this feature for lateral movement or privilege escalation by forwarding stolen tokens.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T03] Direct HTTP API Call Bypass with Credentials in agent_http_bypass.call_direct
findings.detail: This tool allows direct calls to internal resources bypassing security layers, potentially exposing sensitive data or APIs if credentials are provided.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T03] LLM Function Registration with Embedded Credentials in llmchain.register_function
findings.detail: Registers functions that can be called by an LLM, embedding system context and potentially credentials. This could lead to unauthorized access if the function is invoked.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T03] LLM Function Invocation with Context in llmchain.call_with_context
findings.detail: Allows invoking functions registered via LLM, passing context that may contain credentials. This can be exploited to gain unauthorized access.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T03] LLM Context Inspection in llmchain.inspect_context
findings.detail: Allows inspecting the full context passed during function calls, revealing any embedded credentials even if they are not echoed back.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T03] Sub-agent Credential Injection in subchain.spawn_agent
findings.detail: Injects the caller's token into a subprocess environment, allowing the spawned agent to use it without re-authentication. This can be exploited for privilege escalation.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T02] Overly Permissive Input Schema in chain.get_service_manifest
findings.detail: The input schema is overly permissive with no required fields, allowing any user to call this endpoint without restrictions.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T03] Credential Forwarding for Task Delegation in chain.delegate_task
findings.detail: Forwards the caller's token when delegating tasks, potentially allowing an attacker to use this feature for lateral movement or privilege escalation.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T03] Direct HTTP API Call Bypass with Optional Authentication in agent_http_bypass.get_access_log and get_rejected_log
findings.detail: These tools allow reading logs of direct HTTP calls, potentially revealing sensitive information about successful or rejected API requests.

findings.title: [AI] [MCP-T03] Credential Storage in chain.load_agent
findings.detail: Stores the caller's token for future use without issuing a fresh one, potentially exposing credentials to unauthorized access or misuse.

findings.title: [AI] [T1068] Multi-step Exploitation via Unauthenticated Initialization and Prompt Injection
findings.detail: An attacker can exploit the unauthenticated MCP initialization to gain initial access. Then, using prompt injection payloads, they can manipulate the system's behavior or execute arbitrary code.

findings.title: [AI] [T1059] Combination of Excessive Permissions in LLM Chain Tools
findings.detail: The combination of excessive permissions in 'llmchain.register_function', 'llmchain.call_with_context', and 'llmchain.inspect_context' allows an attacker to register dangerous functions, call them with context, and inspect the system context. This can lead to full control over the environment.

findings.title: [AI] [T1059] Exploiting Subchain Spawn Agent for Code Execution
findings.detail: An attacker can exploit 'subchain.spawn_agent' by injecting malicious code into the spawned subprocess, leveraging the lack of input schema and dangerous capabilities like [code_eval] to execute arbitrary commands.

findings.title: [AI] [T1046] Unauthorized Access via Direct HTTP API Calls
findings.detail: With direct HTTP API calls bypassing MCP transport layer security, an attacker can exploit 'agent_http_bypass.call_direct' to perform unauthorized actions or access sensitive data without proper authentication.
